audit.why: EVEN 5.5/10 fits 51.32% over 2309 games: Irelia owns levels 1-5 against a Yasuo who needs two Steel Tempest stacks to knock up, and the lane inverts once he has crit items and Wind Wall to blank her projectiles.

audit.whatIsWrong: Every phases[N].why was the generic Irelia template and none named a Yasuo timing; the level 6 spike claimed Last Breath punishes 'trading CC into his ult range'.
audit.why: Last Breath only blinks to an Airborne target. Irelia's Flawless Duet stuns, it does not knock up, so it does not feed his ultimate. The real level 6 danger is his own two-stack Steel Tempest.
audit.corrected: phases[0..6].why rewritten to Yasuo's actual timings (two-stack Q, Wind Wall 25s/4s, crit spike), spikes[1].text corrected to the Airborne requirement.
sources: enemyKit R text 'Blinks to an Airborne enemy'
ownerKit E text — stun, no knockup

audit.whatIsWrong: The single decisive interaction — Wind Wall blocks BOTH Flawless Duet (E) and Vanguard's Edge (R), which are projectiles — was never stated. The page only said 'nothing works through Wind Wall' generically.
audit.why: Naming which two abilities die to the wall is the whole matchup; it changes when you cast E and R, not just when you step up.
audit.corrected: Written into breakdown.cooldowns, phases[2].why, phases[4].why, phases[6].why, dosFull[2].d and dontsFull[2].d.
sources: ownerKit E and R projectile flags

audit.why: It is the field that carries real cooldowns.
audit.corrected: Wind Wall 25s to 17s for a 4s screen; Sweeping Blade's per-target cooldown is under a second, so he always has a dash if there is a target.

audit.whatIsWrong: CROSS-LAYER DISAGREEMENT: all seven phases[N].side read 'Skill' while win[0..4] read Irelia and win[5]/win[6] read Yasuo.
audit.why: The packet levelChart and every content why agree with the win[] column, so the full layer is the stale side.
audit.corrected: phases[0..4].side set to Irelia and phases[5]/phases[6].side to Yasuo, matching win[] and the packet, with ratings and whys moved in the same group.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was tradeGood verbatim; dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad verbatim (lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED).

audit.corrected: Rewritten to Defiant Dance timing and to off-axis E casting respectively.

edits.before: Q the low minions and keep the blade moving — your level 1 reset dance already out-trades careless mages.
edits.after: Q the low minions and keep the blade moving — Steel Tempest needs two stacks before it knocks you up.

edits.before: W joins: the channel shreds incoming damage — hold it for his trade spell, not his autos.
edits.after: W joins: Defiant Dance cuts physical damage — hold it for the crit auto and his Q.

edits.before: E completes the engine: the stun into stacked-passive autos is half a health bar at 3. Mid lane rarely budgets for it.
edits.after: E completes the engine, but the blades are projectiles: Wind Wall eats them, so make him spend it before you cast.

edits.before: Reset-dance the wave into his face: four stacks, E-stun, Q the kill threat. The lane is a minion-count quiz.
edits.after: Reset-dance the wave into his face: Wind Wall is 25s at rank 1, so his refusal only covers 4 of them.

edits.before: Vanguard's Edge online — the all-in caps with a wall of disengage-proof marks. Dive with the wave as your fuel.
edits.after: Vanguard's Edge online, but it is a projectile — cast it from an angle Wind Wall is not already facing.

edits.before: First item spike: stacked trades delete mages and your sustain mocks their poke math.
edits.after: First item: crit plus the Way of the Wanderer shield out-trades you in a long brawl.

edits.before: Late Irelia surfs the fight: Q-reset through their line, stun the carry pair, and shred whoever peels.
edits.after: Late his Wind Wall blanks your E and R in fights — you need to reach him around it, not through.

edits.before: Last Breath synergizes with your own dash-in engage badly for you — a knocked-up target is now HIS to burst too, so be wary of trading CC into his ult range.
edits.after: Last Breath only blinks to an Airborne target, and your stun is not a knock-up — the danger is his own second Steel Tempest, so break the stack windows.

edits.before: - Yasuo Wind Wall: matchup-defining — Blocks every projectile for its duration — hold your poke until it is spent. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget W Defiant Dance for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - Wind Wall (W) is 25s at rank 1 and 17s at rank 5, and it stands for 4 seconds — Flawless Duet and Vanguard's Edge are both projectiles, so cast neither into it. - Sweeping Blade (E) is off cooldown per target in under a second: he always has a dash.

edits.before: Q-reset through two low minions onto his chest, four-stack autos, E-stun the retreat — the wave-funded all-in he budgeted zero for.
edits.after: Defiant Dance reduces physical damage while charging — hold it for his crit auto and the two-stack Steel Tempest, not his poke.

edits.before: Dashing in under-stacked with W down — Irelia without the engine is a melee minion with a famous haircut.
edits.after: Wind Wall is a 4-second screen he places facing you — throw Flawless Duet off-axis or lose it.

edits.before: Yasuo spends Wind Wall early — the closest thing this matchup has to a guarantee.
edits.after: Vanguard's Edge is a projectile: fire it once Wind Wall's 4 seconds expire.

edits.before: Yasuo wins by landing Wind Wall, denying your pattern, and starting the fight your kit wanted ten seconds later.
edits.after: Yasuo wins by walling your blades, dashing off the wave you left him, and out-critting you once he has items.

edits.before: Carry through the dance — the wave funds dives no cooldown can, and your R turns skirmishes into no-exit interviews.
edits.after: Carry by killing him before crit: Wind Wall covers 4 seconds, and Bladesurge resets outlast every one of them.

edits.before: Ahead, dance louder: crash waves into Yasuo's face, stun the answers, and surf resets through every river fight.
edits.after: Ahead, starve the dash: every minion you deny is a Sweeping Blade target, so freeze short and make him walk to you.

notes: win[0..6] already read Irelia x5 then Yasuo x2 and match the packet levelChart, so the correction here is one-sided: the full-layer phases[].side column was uniformly 'Skill' and was moved onto the content column, not the reverse. No win[] edits accompany the side edits because win[] already carries the target values. Irelia's Flawless Duet carries a 'grounding' derived flag in the kit file, but Riot's own description says only damaged, stunned and Marked — no grounding claim was written anywhere. Yasuo's Last Breath requires an Airborne target and Irelia has no knock-up, so the previous claim that her CC feeds his ultimate was removed.
